questions.text:
निम्नलिखित घटनाओं को कालक्रमानुसार व्यवस्थित कीजिए :
(i) मिखाइल गोर्बाचेव कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी के महासचिव बने
(ii) रूस में समाजवादी क्रांति
(iii) लोगों द्वारा बर्लिन की दीवार तोड़ना
(iv) सोवियत संघ का विघटन
सही विकल्प चुनिए :
questions.text_english:
Arrange the following events in chronological order :
(i) Mikhail Gorbachev became General Secretary of the Communist Party
(ii) Socialist Revolution in Russia
(iii) The Berlin Wall was broken by the people
(iv) Disintegration of the USSR
Choose the correct option :
questions.solution: The correct chronological order is (ii), (i), (iii), (iv) — Option A. The Socialist Revolution in Russia occurred in 1917. Mikhail Gorbachev became General Secretary of the Communist Party in 1985. The Berlin Wall was broken by the people in 1989. The disintegration of the USSR took place in 1991. Options B, C, and D present incorrect sequences that do not match historical timelines.
questions.solution_hindi: सही कालक्रम है (ii), (i), (iii), (iv) — विकल्प A। रूस में समाजवादी क्रांति 1917 में हुई। मिखाइल गोर्बाचेव 1985 में कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी के महासचिव बने। बर्लिन की दीवार 1989 में लोगों द्वारा तोड़ी गई। सोवियत संघ का विघटन 1991 में हुआ।

questions.text: सोवियत संघ के तीन गणराज्यों के उस समूह को चुनिए जिन्होंने यह घोषित किया कि सोवियत संघ समाप्त हो गया।
questions.text_english: Choose the group of three Republics of the USSR which declared that the Soviet Union was disbanded.
questions.solution: The correct answer is Option C — Russia, Ukraine, Belarus. In December 1991, the leaders of these three Slavic republics met at Alma-Ata and signed the Alma-Ata Declaration, formally declaring the dissolution of the Soviet Union and establishing the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS). The other groups mentioned in options A, B, and D are incorrect as Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, Georgia, and Armenia were not part of this founding declaration.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प C है — रूस, यूक्रेन, बेलारूस। दिसंबर 1991 में इन तीन स्लाव गणराज्यों के नेताओं ने अल्मा-अता में मिलकर सोवियत संघ के विघटन की घोषणा की और स्वतंत्र राज्यों के राष्ट्रमंडल (CIS) की स्थापना की।

questions.text:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं :
कथन I : संयुक्त राष्ट्र की स्थापना 1945 में की गई थी।
कथन II : संयुक्त राष्ट्र की स्थापना लीग ऑफ नेशन्स के उत्तराधिकारी के रूप में की गई थी।
उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए :
questions.text_english:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : United Nations was established in 1945.
Statement II : United Nations was founded as a successor to the League of Nations.
In the light of above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.A: कथन I और कथन II दोनों सही हैं।
options.B: कथन I और कथन II दोनों गलत हैं।
options.C: कथन I सही है, परंतु कथन II गलत है।
options.D: कथन I गलत है, परंतु कथन II सही है।

options_english.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
options_english.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
options_english.C: Statement I is true, but Statement II is false.
options_english.D: Statement I is false, but Statement II is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is Option A — Both statements are true. Statement I is correct because the United Nations was formally established on 24 October 1945 after the UN Charter was ratified. Statement II is also correct because the UN was indeed created as a successor to the League of Nations, which had failed to prevent World War II. Both statements are historically accurate and neither contradicts the other.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प A है — दोनों कथन सही हैं। संयुक्त राष्ट्र की स्थापना 24 अक्टूबर 1945 को हुई थी और इसे लीग ऑफ नेशन्स के उत्तराधिकारी के रूप में स्थापित किया गया था जो द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध को रोकने में विफल रहा था।
questions.topic: Formation and Structure of the United Nations

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसको संयुक्त राष्ट्र संघ की एजेंसी नहीं माना जाता है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is not considered as an agency of the UNO?

options.B: संयुक्त राष्ट्र शैक्षणिक, वैज्ञानिक और सांस्कृतिक संगठन (यूनेस्को)

options_english.B: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO)
options_english.C: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)

questions.solution: The correct answer is Option D — World Trade Organisation (WTO). The WTO is an independent international organisation and is not an agency of the United Nations. WHO, UNESCO, and UNHCR are all organs or specialised agencies operating under the United Nations system. The WTO was established in 1995 as a successor to GATT and functions independently of the UN structure.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प D है — विश्व व्यापार संगठन (WTO)। WTO संयुक्त राष्ट्र की एजेंसी नहीं है; यह एक स्वतंत्र अंतरराष्ट्रीय संगठन है जबकि WHO, UNESCO और UNHCR संयुक्त राष्ट्र के अंतर्गत कार्यरत हैं।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित प्रधान मंत्रियों में से किसने भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था की दिशा को तेजी से बदला?
questions.text_english: Who among the following Prime Ministers radically changed the direction of the Indian economy?
questions.solution: The correct answer is Option D — P.V. Narsimha Rao. In 1991, Prime Minister P.V. Narsimha Rao, along with Finance Minister Manmohan Singh, initiated landmark economic reforms that liberalised, privatised, and globalised the Indian economy (LPG reforms). These reforms moved India away from a state-controlled mixed economy toward a market-oriented system. The other leaders did not undertake such fundamental structural changes to the economy.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प D है — पी.वी. नरसिम्हा राव। 1991 में प्रधान मंत्री नरसिम्हा राव ने वित्त मंत्री मनमोहन सिंह के साथ उदारीकरण, निजीकरण और वैश्वीकरण की नीतियाँ लागू कर भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था की दिशा को मूलरूप से बदल दिया।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : आजादी प्राप्त करने के बाद पहली चुनौती भारत की एकता को बनाए रखना था।
कारण (R) : भारत के उप-प्रधान मंत्री एवं गृह मंत्री, सरदार पटेल ने भारत के एकीकरण में महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका अदा की।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : The first challenge after getting independence was to keep India united.
Reason (R) : India's Deputy Prime Minister and the Home Minister, Sardar Patel played an important role in the unification of India.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) को ध्यान से पढ़िए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से सही विकल्प चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the Assertion (A) and Reason (R) carefully and choose the correct option from the options (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परंतु कारण (R) सही है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परंतु कारण (R) गलत है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is Option A — Both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. After independence, maintaining national unity was indeed the foremost challenge as India was deeply fragmented into 562 princely states plus British provinces. Sardar Patel, as Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister, played a decisive role in integrating these princely states through diplomacy and force where necessary, thereby directly addressing the challenge stated in the Assertion. The Reason is thus the correct explanation of the Assertion.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प A है। स्वतंत्रता के बाद एकता बनाए रखना पहली चुनौती थी क्योंकि देश 562 रियासतों में विभाजित था। सरदार पटेल ने गृह मंत्री के रूप में इन रियासतों को एकीकृत किया, जो अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस स्थान पर विस्थापित लोगों की विश्व में सबसे अधिक संख्या पाई जाती है?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following has hosted the world's largest number of displaced people?
questions.solution: The correct answer is Option D — Asia and Pacific. The Asia and Pacific region has historically hosted the largest number of displaced people in the world, primarily due to prolonged conflicts in Afghanistan, Myanmar, and other regional crises. While the Middle East, North Africa, and sub-Saharan Africa also host large displaced populations, the combined scale of displacement in Asia and the Pacific region is the highest globally according to UNHCR data.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प D है — एशिया और प्रशांत। इस क्षेत्र में अफगानिस्तान, म्यांमार और अन्य संघर्षों के कारण विस्थापित लोगों की संख्या सर्वाधिक है।

questions.text: किस भाषा के आधार पर आंध्र प्रदेश का निर्माण किया गया था?
questions.text_english: On the basis of which language was Andhra Pradesh formed?
questions.solution: The correct answer is Option A — Telugu. Andhra Pradesh was carved out of Madras State in 1953 on a linguistic basis to create a separate state for Telugu-speaking people. This happened after a prolonged agitation, most notably by Potti Sriramulu who died after a 58-day fast demanding a separate Telugu state. This creation of Andhra Pradesh led to the reorganisation of states on linguistic lines throughout India.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प A है — तेलुगु। 1953 में तेलुगु भाषी लोगों के लिए मद्रास राज्य से अलग कर आंध्र प्रदेश बनाया गया। पोट्टी श्रीरामुलु के बलिदान के बाद यह राज्य अस्तित्व में आया।

questions.text: भारत का संविधान किस तिथि को अंगीकृत किया गया था?
questions.text_english: On which date was the Constitution of India adopted?
questions.solution: The correct answer is Option B — 26th November, 1949. The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949, which is celebrated as Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) in India. It came into force on 26 January 1950, which is celebrated as Republic Day. The adoption date (26 November) and the enforcement date (26 January) must not be confused.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प B है — 26 नवंबर, 1949। भारत का संविधान संविधान सभा द्वारा 26 नवंबर 1949 को अंगीकृत किया गया था, जिसे संविधान दिवस के रूप में मनाया जाता है। यह 26 जनवरी 1950 को लागू हुआ था।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन भारतीय जनसंघ के बारे में सही नहीं है?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following statements is not true about the Bharatiya Jana Sangh?

options.A: भारत और पाकिस्तान का अखंड भारत में पुनःएकीकरण।
options.B: हिन्दी, भारत की आधिकारिक भाषा हो।
options.C: इसने भारत के द्वारा आणविक हथियारों के विकास का समर्थन किया।
options.D: इसने काँग्रेस के साथ सीमित सहयोग का समर्थन किया।

options_english.A: Reunion of India and Pakistan in Akhand Bharat.
options_english.B: Hindi should be the official language of India.
options_english.C: It advocated that India should develop nuclear weapons.
options_english.D: It advocated limited cooperation with the Congress.

questions.solution: The correct answer is Option D — It advocated limited cooperation with the Congress. This statement is not true about the Bharatiya Jana Sangh. The BJS was a strong opponent of the Congress and did not advocate cooperation with it. Options A, B, and C are all correct positions of the BJS: it championed Akhand Bharat (reunification with Pakistan), promoted Hindi as the official language, and supported India developing nuclear weapons for national security.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प D है। भारतीय जनसंघ कांग्रेस का विरोधी था, न कि सहयोगी। शेष तीन विकल्प — अखंड भारत, हिन्दी को राजभाषा बनाना और परमाणु हथियारों का समर्थन — जनसंघ के वास्तविक दृष्टिकोण थे।

questions.text: उस प्रधान मंत्री का नाम चुनिए जिसने 1989 में नेशनल फ्रंट की सरकार का नेतृत्व किया था।
questions.text_english: Choose the name of the Prime Minister who led the National Front Government in 1989.
questions.solution: The correct answer is Option B — V.P. Singh. After the 1989 general elections, V.P. Singh became the Prime Minister of India leading the National Front coalition government with outside support from the BJP and the Left parties. His government lasted from December 1989 to November 1990. Chandra Shekhar succeeded him briefly, while P.V. Narsimha Rao and H.D. Deve Gowda were Prime Ministers in 1991 and 1996 respectively.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प B है — वी.पी. सिंह। 1989 के आम चुनावों के बाद वी.पी. सिंह ने नेशनल फ्रंट सरकार का नेतृत्व किया। उनकी सरकार दिसंबर 1989 से नवंबर 1990 तक चली।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शस्त्र नियंत्रण का एक उदाहरण नहीं है?
questions.text_english: Which one among the following is not an example of Arms Control?

options.B: सामरिक अस्त्र परिसीमन संधि II (एस.ए.एल.टी. II)

options_english.B: Strategic Arms Limitations Treaty II (SALT II)

questions.solution: The correct answer is Option C — Military Alliance. A military alliance (such as NATO) is a cooperative security arrangement between states, not a mechanism to control or limit arms. Arms control refers to treaties that restrict the development, testing, stockpiling, or deployment of weapons. The ABM Treaty, SALT II, and START are all formal arms control agreements between major powers aimed at limiting their nuclear arsenals. A military alliance does not restrict weapons; it pools them.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प C है — सैन्य गठबन्धन। सैन्य गठबन्धन शस्त्र नियंत्रण का उदाहरण नहीं है। ABM संधि, SALT II और START शस्त्र नियंत्रण की वास्तविक संधियाँ हैं जो परमाणु हथियारों को सीमित करती हैं।

questions.text: क्या प्रथम पंचवर्षीय योजना ने भारत के विकास में सहायता की? दो उदाहरणों की सहायता से अपने मत का समर्थन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Did the First Five Year Plan help in the development of India? Support your opinion with the help of two examples.

key_points: Yes, the First Five Year Plan (1951-56) helped in the development of India.
It focused on agricultural development and irrigation, leading to increased food production and helping India overcome its food crisis.
It also laid the groundwork for large infrastructure projects like dams (Bhakra-Nangal) and river valley projects, boosting energy and irrigation capacity.

questions.solution: Yes, the First Five Year Plan (1951–1956) greatly helped in India's development. First, it prioritised agriculture and irrigation, which significantly increased food grain production and helped India overcome the acute food shortage it faced after Partition. Second, it initiated major infrastructure projects such as the Bhakra-Nangal Dam and other river valley projects that provided irrigation water and hydroelectric power, laying the foundation for industrial and agricultural growth in subsequent plans.

questions.text: यूरोपीय संघ को एक प्रभावशाली क्षेत्रीय संगठन क्यों माना जाता है? कोई दो कारण लिखिए।
questions.text_english: Why is the European Union considered an effective regional organisation? Write any two reasons.

key_points: The EU has a common currency (Euro) and a single integrated market, making it an economic giant capable of challenging even the US in trade matters.
The EU exercises political and diplomatic influence globally and has a common foreign and security policy, enabling member states to coordinate on international issues.

questions.solution: The European Union is considered an effective regional organisation for two major reasons. First, it operates as a single integrated market with a common currency, the Euro, making it one of the world's largest economic blocs that can negotiate on equal terms with the United States and China in trade. Second, the EU has developed a common foreign and security policy, enabling its member states to speak collectively on global issues and exercise significant political and diplomatic influence in international affairs.

questions.text: सुरक्षा के लिए नवीन खतरे के रूप में 'महामारियों' से निपटने के लिए कोई दो उपाय सुझाइए।
questions.text_english: Suggest any two measures to deal with health epidemics as a new threat to security.

key_points: Strengthening international cooperation through organisations like WHO to ensure rapid information sharing, coordinated response, and equitable distribution of medicines and vaccines.
Investing in public health infrastructure, research and development of vaccines, and early warning surveillance systems to detect and contain outbreaks before they spread globally.

questions.solution: To deal with health epidemics as a new security threat, two important measures can be suggested. First, nations must strengthen international cooperation through bodies like the World Health Organisation to enable rapid information sharing, joint research, and equitable distribution of vaccines and medicines. Second, every country should invest in robust public health infrastructure including surveillance systems, trained medical personnel, and emergency response mechanisms to detect outbreaks early and contain their spread before they become global threats.

questions.text: सुरक्षा की पारंपरिक अवधारणा को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain the traditional notion of security.

key_points: Traditional security is concerned primarily with the use or threat of military force between states.
It focuses on protecting a nation's territorial integrity and sovereignty from external military attacks, and the state is both the primary agent and object of security.

questions.solution: The traditional notion of security is primarily concerned with the protection of the state from external military threats. It focuses on the use or threat of military force by one state against another and emphasises safeguarding territorial integrity, sovereignty, and political independence. In this view, the state is both the main provider and the primary object of security. The response to threats involves building military capabilities, forming alliances, and maintaining a balance of power to deter aggression.

questions.text: भारत की विदेश नीति की किन्हीं दो विशेषताओं का वर्णन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Describe any two features of India's foreign policy.

key_points: Non-alignment: India followed a policy of not joining any military bloc during the Cold War, maintaining an independent foreign policy.

Panchsheel: India promoted the five principles of peaceful coexistence — mutual respect for sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality, and peaceful coexistence — as the basis of its foreign relations.

questions.solution: Two key features of India's foreign policy are: First, Non-Alignment — India refused to join either the American-led NATO or the Soviet-led Warsaw Pact blocs during the Cold War, choosing to remain independent in its foreign relations and supporting world peace. Second, Panchsheel — India promoted the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence, which include mutual respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, mutual non-aggression, mutual non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence, as the cornerstone of its bilateral and multilateral relations.

questions.text: पहले तीन आम चुनावों में काँग्रेस पार्टी के प्रभुत्व के कोई दो कारण स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain any two reasons for the dominance of the Congress Party in the first three general elections.

key_points: The Congress had the legacy of the freedom struggle and was associated with nationalist heroes like Gandhi and Nehru, giving it mass appeal and credibility among voters.

The Congress functioned as an umbrella organisation that accommodated diverse social groups, ideologies, and regional interests, making it difficult for any single opposition party to challenge it effectively.

questions.solution: Two important reasons for Congress's dominance in the first three general elections are: First, the Congress Party had the powerful legacy of the independence movement and was closely associated with revered leaders like Mahatma Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru. This gave it enormous public trust, credibility, and emotional appeal among voters across India. Second, the Congress functioned as an umbrella organisation that accommodated diverse ideological groups, castes, communities, and regional interests under one roof, preventing the formation of any united opposition strong enough to challenge its position nationally.

questions.text: 1980 में लोक सभा के मध्यावधि चुनावों की ओर ले जाने वाले किन्हीं दो कारणों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain any two reasons that led to the mid-term elections to the Lok Sabha in 1980.

key_points: The Janata Party government that came to power in 1977 was a coalition of diverse groups united only by their opposition to Indira Gandhi's Emergency, lacking a common ideology or cohesive programme.

Internal conflicts within the Janata Party over the issue of leaders holding dual membership in the RSS led to defections and collapse of the government under Prime Minister Charan Singh, who resigned without facing Parliament.
With no workable majority available for any group, fresh elections were called, resulting in the 1980 mid-term polls.

questions.solution: Two important reasons that led to the mid-term Lok Sabha elections in 1980 are as follows. First, the Janata Party that won the 1977 elections was an ideologically heterogeneous coalition — it included socialists, former Congress members, the Jana Sangh, and Bharatiya Lok Dal — united solely by their opposition to the Emergency. Once in power, they lacked a common programme and were plagued by constant internal rivalry and power struggles among different leaders and factions. Second, a major crisis arose over the question of leaders who continued their membership in the RSS while also holding positions in the Janata government. The Janata Party split when the Charan Singh faction withdrew support, and Charan Singh who briefly became Prime Minister resigned without facing a Parliament confidence vote. With no stable majority possible for any grouping, President Reddy dissolved the Lok Sabha and mid-term elections were announced for January 1980, which Indira Gandhi won with a massive majority.

questions.text: विभाजन के समय देश के कुछ भागों में सांप्रदायिक तनाव और हिंसा को कम करने में महात्मा गाँधी की भूमिका को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain the role of Mahatma Gandhi in reducing communal tension and violence which erupted in some parts of the country at the time of partition.

key_points: Gandhi personally toured riot-affected areas like Noakhali and Calcutta to restore peace and communal harmony.
He undertook fasts unto death to stop communal violence, most notably in Calcutta and Delhi.
He urged Hindus and Muslims to live peacefully together and stood as a symbol of Hindu-Muslim unity.
He insisted on the payment of compensation to Muslims in India and their right to stay safely.

questions.solution: Mahatma Gandhi played a profoundly courageous role in reducing communal tension and violence during Partition. When horrific riots broke out in Noakhali (Bengal) and Bihar, Gandhi personally walked through the affected villages to restore confidence among minorities and appeal for peace. In Calcutta, which was on the brink of large-scale violence in August 1947, Gandhi's presence and his fast unto death moved both communities to halt the killings — what the British called a 'one-man boundary force.' He similarly fasted in Delhi to stop anti-Muslim violence and ensure that Muslims who chose to remain in India were treated with dignity and security. He insisted that the Indian government must pay the dues owed to Pakistan and protect the rights of Muslims in India. His personal sacrifice and moral authority acted as a powerful restraining force on communal passions, even though his tireless efforts ultimately cost him his life when he was assassinated by a fanatic on 30 January 1948.

questions.text: वैश्वीकरण के किन्हीं दो मुख्य कारणों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain any two major causes of globalisation.

key_points: Technological revolution — rapid advances in information technology, the internet, telecommunications, and transportation have shrunk distances and made instantaneous global communication and trade possible.

Liberalisation of economic policies — many countries, especially after the Cold War, opened their markets through reduced trade barriers, privatisation, and deregulation, facilitating the free flow of goods, capital, and services across borders.

questions.solution: Two major causes of globalisation are the following. The first and most significant cause is the technological revolution, particularly in information technology. The development of the internet, satellite communications, and affordable air travel has drastically reduced the costs and time involved in moving goods, services, capital, and ideas across the globe. This has enabled multinational corporations to manage operations across continents and individuals to engage with global markets instantly. The second major cause is the liberalisation of economic policies, especially following the end of the Cold War. Countries around the world, encouraged by institutions like the IMF and WTO, dismantled trade barriers, privatised state enterprises, and opened their economies to foreign investment. This policy shift allowed capital and goods to flow freely across borders, integrating national economies into a single global market and accelerating the process of globalisation.

questions.text_english:
(a) Explain the contribution of any two Non-Governmental Organisations working for the protection of human rights in the world.
OR
(b) Explain the contribution of any two international organisations working for human development and international trade.

sub_questions.text: ऐसे किन्हीं दो गैर-सरकारी संगठनों के योगदान की व्याख्या कीजिए जो विश्व में मानवाधिकारों की रक्षा करने के लिए कार्य कर रहे हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the contribution of any two Non-Governmental Organisations working for the protection of human rights in the world.

key_points: Amnesty International documents and reports human rights abuses worldwide, campaigns for the release of political prisoners, and pressures governments to respect human rights.
Human Rights Watch investigates and exposes human rights violations in conflict zones, works with the media and policymakers to prevent abuses, and advocates for accountability.

sub_questions.solution: Two important NGOs working for human rights protection are: Amnesty International, founded in 1961, works across the world to document violations of human rights including torture, arbitrary detention, and denial of freedom of expression. It campaigns for the release of prisoners of conscience, pressures governments to comply with international human rights law, and raises global awareness through its reports and campaigns. Human Rights Watch is another prominent NGO that conducts field investigations in conflict zones and countries with authoritarian regimes, documenting abuses against civilians. Its detailed reports are used by governments, the UN, and international courts to hold perpetrators accountable and prevent future violations of human rights.

sub_questions.text: ऐसे किन्हीं दो अंतर्राष्ट्रीय संगठनों के योगदान को स्पष्ट कीजिए जो मानव विकास एवं अंतर्राष्ट्रीय व्यापार के लिए काम कर रहे हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the contribution of any two international organisations working for human development and international trade.

key_points: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) promotes human development by providing technical assistance, funding, and expertise to developing nations for education, poverty reduction, and sustainable development.
The World Trade Organisation (WTO) regulates international trade, resolves trade disputes between member nations, and works to lower trade barriers to promote free and fair global trade.

sub_questions.solution: Two important international organisations working for human development and trade are: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) works in over 170 countries to eradicate poverty, reduce inequality, and promote sustainable development. It provides technical assistance, funding, and expertise to help developing nations build human capabilities in areas such as education, health, and governance, and publishes the annual Human Development Report which ranks countries by their Human Development Index. The World Trade Organisation (WTO), established in 1995, governs international trade rules among member nations. It facilitates multilateral trade negotiations to reduce tariffs and trade barriers, provides a dispute settlement mechanism for resolving trade conflicts, and aims to ensure that global trade flows smoothly and predictably, thereby contributing to economic development worldwide.

questions.solution: This question has an internal choice. See sub_questions for model answers to both options (a) and (b).

questions.text_english:
(a) "After the disintegration of the Soviet Union, Indo-Russian relations are gaining new heights." Support the statement with any four examples.
OR
(b) "After the Second World War, the Soviet Union was considered a superpower of the world." Support the statement with any four arguments.

sub_questions.text: "सोवियत संघ के विघटन के बाद, भारत और रूस के संबंध नई ऊँचाइयाँ प्राप्त कर रहे हैं।" इस कथन के पक्ष में कोई चार उदाहरण दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: "After the disintegration of the Soviet Union, Indo-Russian relations are gaining new heights." Support the statement with any four examples.

key_points: Defence cooperation: Russia remains India's largest supplier of defence equipment including aircraft, submarines, and tanks.
Energy cooperation: Russia and India have collaborated in the nuclear energy sector, with Russia helping build the Kudankulam nuclear power plant.
Scientific cooperation: Both countries cooperate in space research and scientific programmes.
Strategic partnership: In 2000, India and Russia signed a Declaration on Strategic Partnership, deepening diplomatic, economic, and security ties.

sub_questions.solution: The statement that Indo-Russian relations have reached new heights after the Soviet Union's disintegration can be supported with four examples. First, in defence cooperation, Russia continues to be India's largest arms supplier, providing advanced military hardware including MiG aircraft, T-90 tanks, INS Vikramaditya aircraft carrier, and S-400 missile defence systems, reflecting deep strategic trust. Second, in energy and nuclear cooperation, Russia has been instrumental in constructing the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant in Tamil Nadu, giving India a boost in civilian nuclear energy capacity. Third, India and Russia signed a Declaration on Strategic Partnership in the year 2000, which was later upgraded to a Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership, institutionalising annual summits and broad bilateral cooperation. Fourth, both nations coordinate their positions in multilateral forums like BRICS, SCO, and the UN on issues of global governance, reflecting shared geopolitical interests and a desire for a multipolar world order.

sub_questions.text: "द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के बाद सोवियत संघ को विश्व की एक महाशक्ति समझा जाता था।" किन्हीं चार तर्कों से इस कथन का समर्थन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: "After the Second World War, the Soviet Union was considered a superpower of the world." Support the statement with any four arguments.

key_points: Military strength: USSR had a massive military force and was the second country after the US to develop nuclear weapons.
Economic strength: The Soviet command economy had achieved rapid industrialisation and high rates of growth, eliminating unemployment.
Political influence: The USSR led the Eastern bloc of socialist countries and had extensive influence over Eastern Europe and parts of Asia and Africa.
Technological achievements: The Soviets launched Sputnik in 1957 and sent the first human into space in 1961, demonstrating technological prowess.

sub_questions.solution: The statement that the Soviet Union was a superpower after the Second World War can be supported with four strong arguments. First, the USSR possessed an enormous military force and became the second nation in the world to develop and test nuclear weapons in 1949, establishing a strategic parity with the United States that defined Cold War politics. Second, the Soviet economy, based on state-owned planning, achieved dramatic industrialisation and eliminated unemployment, enabling it to compete economically with capitalist nations and provide aid to developing countries. Third, the USSR exercised vast political influence, leading a bloc of socialist nations in Eastern Europe, Asia, and elsewhere, and used its UN Security Council veto to shape international outcomes. Fourth, the Soviet Union demonstrated technological and scientific supremacy by launching Sputnik, the world's first artificial satellite, in 1957, and sending Yuri Gagarin as the first human into space in 1961, inspiring other nations and symbolising the superpower status of the USSR.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित अवतरण को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और इस पर आधारित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए :
भारत ने गुट-निरपेक्षता की विदेश नीति को आदर्श माना। संतुलन साधने की यह कठिन कोशिश थी और कभी-कभी संतुलन बहुत कुछ नहीं भी सध पाता था। 1956 में जब ब्रिटेन ने स्वेज़ नहर के मामले को लेकर मिस्र पर आक्रमण किया तो भारत ने इस नव-औपनिवेशिक हमले के विरुद्ध विश्वव्यापी विरोध की अगुवाई की। इसी साल सोवियत संघ ने हंगरी पर आक्रमण किया था लेकिन भारत ने सोवियत संघ के इस कदम की सार्वजनिक निंदा नहीं की। ऐसी स्थिति के बावजूद, कमोबेश भारत ने विभिन्न अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मामलों पर स्वतंत्र रवैया अपनाया। उसे दोनों खेमों के देशों ने सहायता और अनुदान दिए।
questions.text_english: India advocated non-alignment as the ideal foreign policy approach. This was a difficult balancing act and sometimes the balance did not appear perfect. In 1956 when Britain attacked Egypt over the Suez Canal issue, India led the world protest against this neo-colonial invasion. But in the same year when the USSR invaded Hungary, India did not join its public condemnation. Despite such a situation, by and large India did take an independent stand on various international issues and could get aid and assistance from members of both the blocs.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस नेता ने भारत की विदेश नीति की रचना और क्रियान्वयन में महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई थी?
sub_questions.text_english: Who among the following leaders had played a crucial role in the formulation and implementation of India's foreign policy?
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is Option A — Jawaharlal Nehru. As India's first Prime Minister and also the External Affairs Minister, Nehru was the chief architect of India's foreign policy. He articulated the policy of Non-Alignment, championed Panchsheel, and steered India's independent path in international affairs during the Cold War era. The other leaders, while important, did not have the same direct role in shaping independent India's foreign policy.

sub_questions.text: सितम्बर 1961 में गुट-निरपेक्ष आंदोलन की पहली बैठक किस शहर में हुई थी?
sub_questions.text_english: In which city was the first summit of NAM held in September 1961?
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is Option B — Belgrade. The first Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) summit was held in Belgrade, Yugoslavia (present-day Serbia), in September 1961. It was attended by 25 founding member nations. The summit was hosted by Yugoslav leader Josip Broz Tito, along with India's Jawaharlal Nehru and Egypt's Gamal Abdel Nasser, who were the key founders of the movement.

sub_questions.text: उन दो खेमों की पहचान कीजिए जिनसे भारत दूरी बनाए रखना चाहता था।
sub_questions.text_english: Identify the two blocs from whom India wanted to keep a distance.

options.C: संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका और सोवियत संघ

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is Option C — USA and USSR. India's policy of Non-Alignment was specifically designed to keep India free from military or political alignment with either the American-led Western bloc (NATO) or the Soviet-led Eastern bloc (Warsaw Pact). India wanted to maintain an independent foreign policy and not be bound by the obligations or ideological commitments of either superpower, while still receiving assistance from both.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा देश गुट निरपेक्ष आन्दोलन का समर्थक था?
sub_questions.text_english: Which one of the following countries was a supporter of the Non-Aligned Movement?
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is Option D — Egypt. Egypt's President Gamal Abdel Nasser was one of the founding fathers and key supporters of the Non-Aligned Movement along with India's Jawaharlal Nehru and Yugoslavia's Josip Broz Tito. Pakistan was aligned with the USA through SEATO and CENTO, China was part of the communist bloc, and Japan was allied with the United States.

(ii) कर्पूरी ठाकुर से संबंधित राज्य जिन्होंने पिछड़े वर्ग के लिए आरक्षण प्रारंभ किया।

questions.text_english:
In the given political outline map of India (on page 15), four States have been marked as (A), (B), (C) and (D). Identify these States on the basis of the information given below and write their correct names in your answer-book along with the respective serial number of the information used and the concerned alphabets given in the map:
(i) The state where K. Kamaraj was Chief Minister and introduced Mid-day Meal Scheme for school children.
(ii) The state associated with Karpoori Thakur who introduced reservations for the Backward Classes.
(iii) The state where V.V. Giri was a renowned labour leader.
(iv) The state related to Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri.

key_points: (i) → B → Tamil Nadu (K. Kamaraj was Chief Minister of Madras/Tamil Nadu and started the Mid-day Meal Scheme)
(ii) → A → Bihar (Karpoori Thakur was Chief Minister of Bihar and introduced OBC reservations)
(iii) → C → Andhra Pradesh (V.V. Giri was a prominent labour leader from Andhra Pradesh)
(iv) → D → Uttar Pradesh (Lal Bahadur Shastri was from Mughalsarai, Uttar Pradesh)

questions.solution: Based on the map and the clues provided, the four states are identified as follows. (i) Serial number (i) corresponds to map letter B — Tamil Nadu. K. Kamaraj was the Chief Minister of Madras (later Tamil Nadu) and pioneered the Mid-day Meal Scheme for school children, which later became a model for the entire country. (ii) Serial number (ii) corresponds to map letter A — Bihar. Karpoori Thakur, popularly known as 'Jan Nayak', was the Chief Minister of Bihar and is celebrated for introducing reservations for Other Backward Classes (OBC) in the state. (iii) Serial number (iii) corresponds to map letter C — Andhra Pradesh. V.V. Giri was a distinguished labour leader and trade unionist from Andhra Pradesh who later became the President of India. (iv) Serial number (iv) corresponds to map letter D — Uttar Pradesh. Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri was born in Mughalsarai (now Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Nagar), Uttar Pradesh, and is therefore associated with this state.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा वैध कारण चीन का प्रतिनिधित्व करने के लिए 'साइकिल' को चुनने के लिए सही है?
sub_questions.text_english: Which one of the following is the valid reason to choose 'cycle' to represent China?

options.A: साइकिल का प्रयोग करने में चीन विश्व का सबसे अग्रणी देश है।
options.B: यह चीन की कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी का प्रतीक चिह्न है।
options.C: यह चीन की गरीबी को दर्शाती है।
options.D: चीन में साइकिल चलाना एक लोकप्रिय खेल है।

options_english.A: China is the largest user of cycles in the world.
options_english.B: It is the symbol of Communist Party of China.
options_english.D: Popularity of cycling as a sport in China.

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is Option A — China is the largest user of cycles in the world. The bicycle is chosen to represent China because China has historically been the world's largest manufacturer and user of bicycles. The cycle is a culturally significant symbol of everyday Chinese life and transport. It does not specifically symbolise the Communist Party, nor does it indicate poverty; rather, it reflects China's identity as the dominant cycling nation.

sub_questions.text: साइकिल के पिछले पहिये में 'डालर' क्या दर्शाता है?
sub_questions.text_english: What does the dollar in the rear wheel of the cycle depict?

options.A: चीन पर अमरीकी अर्थव्यवस्था का प्रभाव
options.B: दोनों के बीच आधे-आधे की भागीदारी
options.C: चीन की अमरीकी अर्थव्यवस्था पर निर्भरता
options.D: अमरीका द्वारा चीन को दी गई आर्थिक सहायता

options_english.A: The influence of the US economy on China
options_english.B: Fifty percent partnership of the two
options_english.C: Dependence of China on US economy
options_english.D: Economic aid to China by US

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is Option A — The influence of the US economy on China. The dollar symbol in the rear wheel of the bicycle representing China depicts the significant influence that the American economy (and by extension, US capital and global financial systems) has had on China's economic transformation. After Deng Xiaoping's reforms, China opened up to foreign investment and trade, particularly with the USA, making the US economy a major driver of China's growth.

sub_questions.text: चीन में प्रारम्भिक वर्षों में किस प्रकार की अर्थव्यवस्था थी?
sub_questions.text_english: Which form of economy was popular initially in China?
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is Option C — Socialist. After the Communist revolution in 1949 under Mao Zedong, China adopted a socialist economic model based on state ownership of the means of production, central planning, and collectivisation of agriculture. All major industries were nationalised and the economy was directed by the state rather than the market. China only began shifting toward a market-oriented system after Deng Xiaoping's reforms in 1978.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा विकल्प कार्टून द्वारा दिए गए सन्देश की सबसे सही अभिव्यक्ति है?
sub_questions.text_english: Which one of the following option is the most appropriate message given by the cartoon?

options.A: चीन केवल अमरीकी अर्थव्यवस्था के लिए खुला है।
options.B: चीन ने अमरीका के साथ व्यापारिक सम्बन्ध स्थापित कर लिए हैं।
options.C: चीन केवल यूरोपीय देशों के साथ कार्य करता है।
options.D: चीन ने डालर को अपनी मुद्रा बना लिया है।

options_english.A: China is open only to US economy.
options_english.B: China has established trade relations with US.
options_english.C: China works only with European countries.
options_english.D: China has adopted dollar as its currency.

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is Option B — China has established trade relations with US. The cartoon's most appropriate overall message is that China, while retaining its own identity (the bicycle), has integrated itself into the global capitalist economy and established strong trade relations with the United States (symbolised by the dollar in the wheel). The dollar does not mean China has abandoned its identity; rather, it has blended its traditional model with market economics through US trade engagement.

questions.text:
(क) सार्क के सदस्य देशों के बीच सहयोग के किन्हीं दो क्षेत्रों तथा संघर्ष के किन्हीं दो क्षेत्रों का वर्णन कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) ऐसी किन्हीं तीन घटनाओं का वर्णन कीजिए जो यह दर्शाती हैं कि सभी दक्षिण एशियाई देशों के लोग अपने देश में लोकतंत्र की स्थापना चाहते हैं।
questions.text_english:
(a) Describe any two areas of cooperation and any two areas of conflict among the member countries of the SAARC.
OR
(b) Describe any three events that show that people of all the South Asian countries want to have democracy in their country.

sub_questions.text: सार्क के सदस्य देशों के बीच सहयोग के किन्हीं दो क्षेत्रों तथा संघर्ष के किन्हीं दो क्षेत्रों का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe any two areas of cooperation and any two areas of conflict among the member countries of the SAARC.

key_points: Areas of cooperation: Trade liberalisation through SAFTA; cooperation in disaster management and cultural exchanges.
Areas of conflict: India-Pakistan territorial disputes over Kashmir; cross-border terrorism affecting bilateral and regional relations.

sub_questions.solution:
Two areas of cooperation among SAARC member countries are: First, economic cooperation through the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) agreement, which aims to reduce tariffs and boost intra-regional trade among member states. SAARC countries also collaborate on agriculture, science and technology, and cultural exchanges to foster mutual goodwill. Second, humanitarian and disaster management cooperation — SAARC members, who share common vulnerabilities to natural disasters like floods and earthquakes, have established frameworks for emergency relief and coordination, which was strengthened through the SAARC Disaster Management Centre.

Two major areas of conflict are: First, the unresolved dispute over Kashmir remains the most significant source of tension between India and Pakistan, preventing deeper regional integration and often derailing SAARC summit meetings. Second, cross-border terrorism and the related issues of infiltration and insurgency have severely strained the relationship between India and its neighbours, particularly Pakistan, making it difficult to build comprehensive trust and cooperation within the SAARC framework.

sub_questions.text: ऐसी किन्हीं तीन घटनाओं का वर्णन कीजिए जो यह दर्शाती हैं कि सभी दक्षिण एशियाई देशों के लोग अपने देश में लोकतंत्र की स्थापना चाहते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe any three events that show that people of all the South Asian countries want to have democracy in their country.

key_points: Nepal's pro-democracy movements against the monarchy ultimately led to the restoration of democracy and later the abolition of the monarchy.
Pakistan's repeated struggles against military dictatorships, with civilian parties and civil society continually demanding restoration of democratic governance.
Bangladesh's movement against military ruler Ershad in 1990 resulted in the restoration of parliamentary democracy.

sub_questions.solution: Three events demonstrating that people of South Asian countries desire democracy are: First, in Nepal, a popular pro-democracy movement in 1990 forced King Birendra to accept multiparty democracy. Later, the Jana Andolan II movement of 2006 compelled King Gyanendra to restore Parliament after he had suspended it, eventually leading to Nepal's transformation into a federal democratic republic, showing the deep popular desire for representative governance. Second, in Pakistan, despite repeated military coups — by Ayub Khan, Yahya Khan, Zia ul-Haq, and Pervez Musharraf — the Pakistani people and political parties have consistently fought to restore civilian democratic rule. The movement against Pervez Musharraf's dictatorship in 2007–08 and the eventual return to civilian government illustrate this persistent democratic aspiration. Third, in Bangladesh, a mass uprising in 1990 against military ruler General Ershad forced him to resign. Following his fall, Bangladesh held free multiparty elections and has since maintained a parliamentary democratic system, reflecting the public's firm commitment to democratic governance over authoritarian rule.

questions.text:
(क) "साझे परंतु अलग-अलग उत्तरदायित्वों के बावजूद, मानवीय अस्तित्व को चुनौती देने वाली पर्यावरणीय समस्याएँ दिन-ब-दिन बढ़ती जा रही हैं।" इस स्थिति के लिए उत्तरदायी किन्हीं चार कारणों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) वैश्विक पर्यावरण के संरक्षण में भारत की भूमिका का आकलन इसके द्वारा लिए गए किन्हीं चार कदमों के आधार पर कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) "Despite common but differentiated responsibilities, the environmental problems are increasing day-by-day challenging human existence." Analyse any four reasons responsible for this situation.
OR
(b) Assess India's role to protect the global environment on the basis of any four steps taken by it.

sub_questions.text: "साझे परंतु अलग-अलग उत्तरदायित्वों के बावजूद, मानवीय अस्तित्व को चुनौती देने वाली पर्यावरणीय समस्याएँ दिन-ब-दिन बढ़ती जा रही हैं।" इस स्थिति के लिए उत्तरदायी किन्हीं चार कारणों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: "Despite common but differentiated responsibilities, the environmental problems are increasing day-by-day challenging human existence." Analyse any four reasons responsible for this situation.

key_points: Rapid industrialisation and urbanisation leading to increased greenhouse gas emissions.
Deforestation for agriculture and development destroying carbon sinks.
Unequal power dynamics where developed nations resist binding commitments while developing nations prioritise economic growth.
Lack of effective international enforcement mechanisms for environmental agreements.

sub_questions.solution: Four reasons responsible for the worsening of global environmental problems are: First, rapid industrialisation and urbanisation, especially in emerging economies, have led to a massive increase in the burning of fossil fuels, releasing greenhouse gases like CO2 and methane that accelerate climate change and global warming. Second, widespread deforestation for agriculture, mining, and infrastructure development has destroyed critical carbon sinks such as tropical rainforests, reducing the earth's capacity to absorb carbon dioxide and resulting in biodiversity loss. Third, there is a fundamental disagreement between developed and developing nations over the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities. Developed countries that historically contributed most to emissions are reluctant to bear greater financial burdens, while developing countries insist on their right to grow economically, creating a deadlock in meaningful global action. Fourth, existing international environmental agreements like the Kyoto Protocol lack strong enforcement mechanisms; nations can withdraw from commitments (as the USA did from the Kyoto Protocol) without facing significant consequences, making global environmental governance ineffective in practice.

sub_questions.text: वैश्विक पर्यावरण के संरक्षण में भारत की भूमिका का आकलन इसके द्वारा लिए गए किन्हीं चार कदमों के आधार पर कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Assess India's role to protect the global environment on the basis of any four steps taken by it.

key_points: India signed and ratified the Paris Agreement on climate change in 2016 and committed to reducing the emissions intensity of its GDP.
India has launched the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) with missions on solar energy, energy efficiency, and sustainable habitat.
India is one of the largest installers of renewable energy, particularly solar, and committed to the International Solar Alliance.
India signed and ratified the Convention on Biological Diversity and has taken steps to protect its forests, wildlife, and natural habitats.

sub_questions.solution: India has taken several important steps to protect the global environment. First, India signed and ratified the Paris Agreement in 2016 and made ambitious Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) committing to reduce the emissions intensity of its GDP by 45% by 2030 from 2005 levels and to achieve 50% of its cumulative electric power from non-fossil fuel sources. Second, India launched the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) in 2008, comprising eight national missions including the Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission, the National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency, and the National Water Mission. Third, India is a co-founder of the International Solar Alliance (ISA) launched jointly with France in 2015, aimed at promoting solar energy among sun-rich countries. India has also massively expanded its renewable energy capacity, becoming one of the top renewable energy producers in the world. Fourth, India has ratified the Convention on Biological Diversity and the Kyoto Protocol, demonstrating its international commitment. Domestically, India has expanded protected area networks, undertaken afforestation drives, and enacted environmental legislation to conserve biodiversity and reduce pollution, reflecting its serious commitment to global environmental protection.

questions.text:
(क) 1979 से 1985 तक असम में बाहरी लोगों के विरुद्ध चले आंदोलन के किन्हीं तीन कारणों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) 1967 से 1985 तक पंजाब में अशान्ति और हिंसा के किन्हीं तीन कारणों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Analyse any three reasons for the movement against outsiders in Assam from 1979 to 1985.
OR
(b) Analyse any three reasons for the unrest and violence in Punjab from 1967 to 1985.

sub_questions.text: 1979 से 1985 तक असम में बाहरी लोगों के विरुद्ध चले आंदोलन के किन्हीं तीन कारणों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Analyse any three reasons for the movement against outsiders in Assam from 1979 to 1985.

key_points: Large-scale illegal migration from Bangladesh, which Assamese people felt was changing the demographic composition and threatening their cultural and linguistic identity.
Economic anxiety — migrants were perceived as taking jobs, land, and resources away from the indigenous Assamese population.
Political concerns — the influx of migrants was seen as distorting the electoral rolls and giving outsiders undue political influence in Assam.

sub_questions.solution: Three major reasons for the anti-outsider movement in Assam from 1979 to 1985 are: First, the large-scale and continuing migration of people from Bangladesh into Assam created deep anxiety among the indigenous Assamese people, who feared that their cultural, linguistic, and ethnic identity was being diluted. This fear of becoming a minority in their own homeland was a powerful motivating force behind the Assam Movement led by the All Assam Students' Union (AASU). Second, the economic dimension of the crisis was equally significant. Migrants were perceived as competing for scarce land, agricultural employment, and business opportunities, depriving the local Assamese population of economic resources and livelihoods. This economic competition generated resentment and gave the movement a mass base across different sections of Assamese society. Third, the political implications of migration were deeply alarming to Assamese leaders. The names of illegal migrants appeared on electoral rolls, which the Assamese believed was manipulating elections, giving outsiders disproportionate political power, and electing leaders who were not representative of genuine Assamese interests. The demand to update the National Register of Citizens and remove illegal migrants' names from voter lists was central to the movement, which culminated in the Assam Accord of 1985.

sub_questions.text: 1967 से 1985 तक पंजाब में अशान्ति और हिंसा के किन्हीं तीन कारणों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Analyse any three reasons for the unrest and violence in Punjab from 1967 to 1985.

key_points: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution of 1973 demanded greater autonomy for Punjab and recognition of Sikh religious identity, which led to a political impasse with the central government.
The rise of Bhindranwale and armed extremism fuelled violence and targeted killings in Punjab.
The territorial disputes over Chandigarh, river waters (Ravi-Beas), and Hindi-speaking areas between Punjab and Haryana remained unresolved, adding to Sikh grievances.

sub_questions.solution: Three important reasons for the unrest and violence in Punjab from 1967 to 1985 are: First, the political and religious grievances of the Sikh community crystallised in the Anandpur Sahib Resolution of 1973, passed by the Akali Dal, which demanded greater regional autonomy for Punjab within the Indian Union, recognition of Sikh rights, and resolution of territorial disputes with Haryana. The central government's failure to adequately address these demands fuelled a sense of political alienation among Sikhs. Second, the rise of Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale transformed political discontent into violent militancy. Bhindranwale and his followers took refuge in the Golden Temple complex in Amritsar, from where they directed targeted killings of political opponents and Hindu leaders. The government's Operation Blue Star in 1984 to flush them out resulted in massive casualties and deeply wounded Sikh religious sentiment, intensifying the cycle of violence. Third, unresolved territorial and resource disputes — including the question of which city (Chandigarh) would be Punjab's capital, the distribution of river waters of the Ravi and Beas between Punjab and Haryana, and the transfer of Hindi-speaking areas to Haryana — remained festering sources of grievance. These economic and political disputes convinced many Sikhs that their interests were being systematically ignored, radicalising sections of the population and sustaining the violent movement.

questions.text:
(क) 1990 के दशक में भारतीय राजनीति के किन्हीं चार नए रुझानों का वर्णन कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) 1989 के बाद की किन्हीं चार घटनाओं का वर्णन कीजिए जिनका भारत की राजनीति पर दीर्घकालिक प्रभाव हुआ।
questions.text_english:
(a) Describe any four new trends of Indian politics that can be noticed during the decade of 1990s.
OR
(b) Describe any four developments after 1989 that had a long lasting impact on Indian politics.

sub_questions.text: 1990 के दशक में भारतीय राजनीति के किन्हीं चार नए रुझानों का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe any four new trends of Indian politics that can be noticed during the decade of 1990s.

key_points: Rise of coalition politics as no single party could win a majority, requiring multiple parties to form governments.
Emergence of regional parties as powerful political actors capable of influencing national politics.
Rise of OBC and Dalit politics following the Mandal Commission recommendations, transforming the social base of Indian democracy.
Increased communal polarisation following the Babri Masjid demolition in 1992 and the Ram Janmabhoomi movement.

sub_questions.solution: Four new trends of Indian politics in the 1990s are: First, the era of coalition politics began as the Congress Party's dominant position weakened after 1989. No single party could win a clear majority, leading to unstable coalition governments at the Centre — from the National Front under V.P. Singh to the United Front and finally the BJP-led NDA — establishing coalition as the new normal of Indian governance. Second, regional parties gained unprecedented national importance. Parties like the Samajwadi Party, BSP, Telugu Desam Party, DMK, and AIADMK became kingmakers at the Centre, reflecting the federal diversity of Indian polity and the growing assertion of state-level identities. Third, the Mandal Commission controversy in 1990 unleashed a powerful wave of backward caste politics. The implementation of OBC reservations by V.P. Singh transformed the social composition of political mobilisation, bringing new social groups from OBC and Dalit communities to the centre of political life and challenging upper-caste dominance. Fourth, the demolition of the Babri Masjid in December 1992 and the BJP's rise on the platform of Hindutva and Ram Janmabhoomi introduced a strong element of religious mobilisation into mainstream politics, fundamentally altering the ideological landscape and deepening communal polarisation in Indian society.

sub_questions.text: 1989 के बाद की किन्हीं चार घटनाओं का वर्णन कीजिए जिनका भारत की राजनीति पर दीर्घकालिक प्रभाव हुआ।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe any four developments after 1989 that had a long lasting impact on Indian politics.

key_points: The end of Congress dominance and the beginning of the coalition era changed the nature of Indian democracy permanently.
The economic reforms of 1991 (LPG reforms) under Narasimha Rao transformed the economic framework and created new political constituencies around market liberalisation.
The Mandal Commission implementation empowered backward classes and fundamentally altered the social basis of Indian electoral politics.
The Babri Masjid demolition in 1992 and the rise of the BJP-led NDA to power in 1999 demonstrated the long-term electoral impact of the Hindutva movement.

sub_questions.solution: Four major post-1989 developments with long-lasting impact on Indian politics are: First, the collapse of Congress majority in 1989 permanently ended one-party dominance and ushered in the era of coalition governance. Every government since 1989 has been either a coalition or a minority government, fundamentally changing how power is negotiated and exercised in Indian democracy. Second, the economic liberalisation of 1991 under Prime Minister Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Manmohan Singh opened India's economy and set it on a path of high growth. This created new middle-class constituencies, empowered business groups, and over time shifted political discourse toward economic performance, competitiveness, and aspiration as central electoral issues. Third, the Mandal Commission implementation in 1990 by V.P. Singh set in motion a durable social revolution in Indian politics. It mobilised the numerically large OBC communities and led to the rise of powerful OBC-based parties and leaders, permanently altering the caste calculus of elections across north and central India. Fourth, the Ram Janmabhoomi movement culminating in the Babri Masjid demolition in December 1992 had far-reaching political consequences. It damaged the secular consensus, fuelled communal violence, and over the long term contributed to the BJP's growth into a dominant political force, eventually forming the NDA government in 1999 and transforming the competitive landscape of Indian national politics.
